about: The museum lists Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer 4D at 4, 4:45, 5:15, 5:45, 6:15 and 7:30 PM, and the Aróra planetarium show at 4:30, 5:30 and 6:15 PM. The 5:30 Aróra and 6:15 Rudolph showings include American Sign Language interpretation.

Extended evening hours let families explore the museum galleries and the Boeing Observatory, weather permitting. The host adds that general admission covers four floors of permanent exhibits and the observatory.

At the end of the evening the museum officially lights the planetarium dome with a holiday display. Proceeds from pay as you may admission support the South Carolina State Museum Foundation and its educational programs.

Outside this special evening, the museum is open Tuesday through Saturday from 10 AM to 5 PM and Sunday from noon to 5 PM, and it is closed Mondays. Show tickets can be bought ahead on the museum's ticketing site.
faq: How much is admission?
General admission is pay as you may that evening, and planetarium and 4D shows are $5 for the public or $4 for members.
When is the event?
Tuesday, December 1, 2026, from 4 to 8:30 PM at the South Carolina State Museum.
Is it accessible?
The museum lists wheelchair accessibility and ASL interpretation at select shows.

about: The Holiday Market runs Thursday through Saturday from 9:30 AM to 5 PM and Sunday from noon to 4 PM in the Goodman and Cantey buildings. The host says more than 140 merchants take part and the market is the Junior League of Columbia's largest annual fundraiser.
Sundaes with Santa runs Sunday from noon to 3 PM, and the host notes Santa returns to the North Pole one hour before the market closes at 4 PM. Tickets are sold at the door.
General admission tickets are valid for return visits all weekend, and children 12 and under are free during regular shopping hours. Parking is $5 and food and drinks are sold during market hours.
faq: How much is Sundaes with Santa?
The host lists $8 per child and $10 per adult, with tickets at the door.
Are Santa photos free?
Yes, photos are free, but families bring their own camera.
Where do I park?
Enter Gate 6 at 901 George Rogers Blvd, and parking is $5.
Is there food at the market?
Food and beverages are sold during regular market hours.
Can kids shop for free?
Children 12 and under are free during regular shopping hours, but not at the special Santa event.

about: The town describes the tree lighting as a beloved community tradition held each December in Whitt Cline Community Park. Neighbors gather under the twinkling lights to celebrate the season.
Local school choirs and bands perform, and Mayor Danielson gives a greeting before the crowd counts down to the lighting. The host contact for the event is listed as pbrewer@townofirmosc.com.
Treats afterward include pizza, hot chocolate and cookies. Santa arrives as the fire truck sirens sound, and children rush to greet him and share Christmas wishes.
The page frames the evening as a way for neighbors to gather and celebrate the holiday season, so it works as a short, low-key stop for young children before bedtime.
Mayor Danielson's greeting comes before the tree is lit, and the town says the crowd waits for the countdown to see the tree glow over the park.
faq: When is the Irmo tree lighting?
Tuesday, December 1, 2026, at 6 PM.
Where is it?
Whitt Cline Community Park, 7330 Carlisle St, Irmo.
Does Santa come?
Yes, the town says Santa arrives by fire truck after the lighting.
What food is served?
The town lists pizza, hot chocolate and cookies after the lighting.
Who performs?
Local school choirs and bands, per the town's page.
Who do I contact?
The town page lists pbrewer@townofirmosc.com.
Is there a price?
The town page prints no price, so the cost is shown as not listed.
What is the order of the evening?
School choirs and bands and the mayor's greeting come first, then the countdown and tree lighting, then treats and Santa's arrival.

about: The Snowball Festival carries a free admission listing for the carnival day, with doors at 11 AM and activities until 3 PM. The venue says the event goes on rain or shine.

The vendor list names Tally Ho Mobile Petting Zoo, Carolina Holiday Mini Golf, Balloonopolis face painting and balloon animals, Palmetto Amusements, The Haute Dog Lady, Brain Freeze and Blankets of Hope. Vendors are subject to change.
Seating is blankets and low lawn seating only, and the venue lists limited ADA seating and parking.
faq: Is the carnival free?
The Icehouse Amphitheater lists free admission.
Can I bring chairs?
No freestanding chairs are allowed, only blankets and low lawn seating.
Can I bring food?
The venue does not permit outside food or drink, and vendors are on site.
Is the petting zoo included?
The venue lists Tally Ho Mobile Petting Zoo among the vendors, and vendors are subject to change.
Are there cookies?
The venue promises free cookies.

about: The library lists the program as in person on Wednesday, December 16, 2026, from 5:30 to 6:30 PM at the Gaston Branch Library. It is filed under the Holidays category.
The audience tags include preschool, elementary, middle school, high school and families, though the host says the visit is for families with children.
The event page does not print a price or a registration requirement, so the cost is shown as not listed here.

The same Family Palooza holiday series from Lexington County Public Library also lists Grinchy Claus Day at the Chapin Branch on December 3 and a Visit With Santa at the South Congaree Branch on December 11, so families can pick the branch closest to home.
The library catalogs the program as in person only, with an hour-long slot that starts at 5:30 PM, which suits families coming straight from school or work.
faq: When is the Santa visit?
Wednesday, December 16, 2026, from 5:30 to 6:30 PM.
Where is it?
Gaston Branch Library, 214 S Main St, Gaston.
Who is it for?
The host says families with children.
Do I need to register?
The event page prints no registration requirement, so check with the branch before you go.
What happens at the visit?
Children meet Santa, share a wish list and take a festive photo, according to the library.
Is it in person?
Yes, the library lists it as an in-person program.
